deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'tame' (modérée) geometry. A 'structure modérée' is a system M_* = (M_n)_n, where M_n is a family of subsets of R^n, subject to axioms M1–M4 given on earlier pages. A 'moderate space' is a set X with a moderate structure, essentially an equivalence class of injections X -> R^n with image in M_n. Moderate maps are presumably those whose graphs are moderate. The category is Esp_{M_*}. This is the precursor of what later became 'o-minimal structures / definable sets' (and of the axiomatic structures of van den Dries, Shiota and others).

On this page he adds axiom (M5): for every n, M_n is stable under finite unions, equivalently ∅ ∈ M_n and A, B ∈ M_n ⇒ A ∪ B ∈ M_n. He draws three consequences.
(1) The moderate parts of a moderate space are stable under finite unions.
(2) ∅ carries a unique moderate structure, and it is an initial object of Esp_{M_*}. The empty function has empty graph, which is moderate by M5.
(3) If (X_i)_{i∈I} is a finite family of moderate parts of X, then ∪X_i is a moderate part. If X = ∪X_i, then X is the colimit (somme amalgamée) of the diagram of the X_i glued along the X_i ∩ X_j. Equivalently, a map f: X -> Y between moderate spaces is moderate iff all f|X_i are. Proof: graph(f) = ∪ graph(f|X_i), which is moderate by M5. Conversely, compatible moderate maps on the X_i glue set-theoretically to a map whose graph is a finite union of moderate sets.

He then poses a question. Given a span X_1 <- Z -> X_2 in Esp_{M_*}, does a pushout exist? When the apex is empty this is the question of finite coproducts. The next page answers it: the pushout exists and commutes with the forgetful functor X -> |X| iff there is a finite family of moderate functions f_α on X_1 and g_α on X_2 that agree on Z and jointly embed the set-theoretic pushout into R^A. The previous page proves that if the set-theoretic colimit of a finite diagram admits a moderate structure making the canonical maps moderate, it is the colimit. The aim is to understand gluing / finite colimits of tame spaces, i.e. to build 'abstract' moderate spaces by gluing affine ones, as with definable spaces in o-minimality.
errors: In the last line 'Si Y = ∅' should read 'Si Z = ∅' (the apex of the span). This is a slip of notation.

The equivalence in (3) tacitly uses that restriction of a moderate map to a moderate part is moderate, and that moderate maps are characterized by moderate graphs. Both presumably come from axioms M1–M4 on earlier pages; this is not a real gap.

Whether finite coproducts exist actually depends on axioms not stated here: one needs something like X×{0} ∪ Y×{1} ⊂ R^{n+1} to be in M_{n+1}, i.e. products with points or translations. Grothendieck rightly leaves it as a question at this axiomatic level.

ideas.what: Axiom M5: each M_n closed under finite unions (including ∅) in an axiomatic tame-geometry structure
ideas.modern_name: Boolean-closure axiom of o-minimal / tame structures on (R^n)_n
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (1984–86), Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight; also Shiota's axiomatics
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for tame topology but gives no such axiomatics

ideas.what: Empty set as initial object; a finite cover by moderate parts is a colimit (gluing lemma via graphs)
ideas.modern_name: Finite definable covers are colimits in the category of definable sets/spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in o-minimal geometry (van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal structures, 1998, ch. 10 definable spaces)

ideas.what: Existence of pushouts/finite coproducts in the category of moderate spaces, with a criterion via a finite separating family of moderate functions (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / finite colimits of definable sets; affineness of the gluing
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal literature (van den Dries 1998; definable spaces gluing), Robson for semialgebraic spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats tame geometry categorically from the outset, asking for finite colimits in Esp_{M_*} and for when the forgetful functor to sets preserves them. The o-minimal literature developed this only implicitly (definable spaces by gluing). This documents an independent axiomatics predating or parallel to van den Dries, but the content on this page is routine.
missed.quote: Donnons-nous X_1 <- Z -> X_2 dans Esp_{M_*}, existe-t-il une somme amalgamée ? Si [Z] = ∅, c'est la question de l'existence des sommes finies
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's early axiomatic tame topology. The mathematics is standard in o-minimality now.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is elementary axiomatics (closure under finite unions, initial object, gluing along finite covers) plus a natural question about pushouts. The historical interest is that it is an independent early axiomatics of what became o-minimal structures, but nothing here is mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: 'Ens_{M_n}' should be read as 'Esp_{M_*}' (category of moderate spaces), consistent with the previous page.
'Si Y = ∅' is in the manuscript but is a slip for Z (the apex); the transcription is faithful otherwise.
Second 'Proposition' line: 'qui en fait objet initial de Esp_{M_*}'.
'(⇔ ∅ ∈ M_n, & A, B ∈ M_n ⇒ A ∪ B ∈ M_n)': the stray 'et' after '&' is likely not in the manuscript.
